{"id": "27def70e-d9b1-41fe-9cdc-4a90ed4645f9", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — missing CacheHitRate datapoints shouldn't be reported as 0%.

CacheHitRate is a sparse CloudWatch metric: CloudFront only publishes a datapoint when there were actual viewer requests in that period. If there's no traffic hitting the distribution (or it's not receiving requests during the window reviewed), CloudWatch simply has nothing to report — there's no "0" value emitted, just an absence of data.

Reporting it as a 0% cache hit rate would misrepresent the situation as "every request was a miss," when the real story is "no requests occurred" (or at least none that CloudFront measured for that metric in that window). For an operational review, it's more accurate to state something like: "No CacheHitRate datapoints were returned for the period, indicating no measured viewer requests — not a 0% hit rate."

If you want, I can check whether the distribution actually had any request volume (e.g., via Requests or BytesDownloaded metrics) during the review window to confirm whether this is a true traffic gap or just a metric reporting quirk.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
